plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE with limma-trend + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The core facility delivered log2(TPM+1) normalized expression (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 treated, 6 control, single batch, unpaired), not raw counts. This rules out count-based models (DESeq2/edgeR/voom) and requires limma-trend, which is the consensus method for log-scale abundance data (limma User's Guide; Ritchie et al. 2015; rule R-0019). The plan proceeds: (1) QC on the log-abundance matrix itself (no re-transform) via PCA/MDS and sample-distance heatmap to confirm the two groups separate and to catch any outlier before modeling; (2) a mean-log-expression filter (no re-normalization, since values are already normalized log2 TPM) with an explicit floor and an independent-of-labels criterion, minimum detected in >= 6 samples (the smaller group size); (3) an explicit factor releveling (control as reference) and named contrast treatment-control so fold-change direction is unambiguous; (4) limma linear model with eBayes(trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE) to fit the mean-variance trend of log-scale data and guard against hypervariable genes; (5) BH-adjusted topTable output, selecting DE genes by adjusted p-value (padj < 0.05), not by fold change or raw p-value alone; (6) fgsea preranked GSEA on the moderated t-statistic (the log-scale-data analog of a Wald statistic, since no DESeq2 Wald stat exists here) against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally, 2026.1) as primary and Reactome pathways (staged locally) as a secondary pass, gene sets windowed to 15-500 members, with camera as a correlation-aware cross-check on the same limma fit; (7) a consolidated report with full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene set collection versions, design, thresholds, n tested/n DE, leading-edge genes per significant set) and an explicit statement that enrichment results are method-dependent.
